title: Jittered timeout + escape handoff for continuous-batcher scheduler
author: Claire Nguyen
description:
Context: Continuous-batcher starvation and occasional head-of-line blocking have been a source of intermittent p99 spikes under mixed KV-heavy and small-chat workloads. This PR introduces a two-part mitigation: 1) jittered timeout escape that prevents synchronized timeouts across many slots, and 2) an escape-handoff path that proactively routes long-waiting KV-heavy requests to a reserved lightweight execution path to avoid starving short low-token requests.

Motivation: Prior approaches (strict deadlines or static reservation) either introduced throughput loss or complex tuning. We observed periodic waves where many slots hit the same requeue deadline and then contended for kernel resources, amplifying tail latency. Adding small randomized offsets (jitter) reduces global synchronization; the handoff prevents prolonged KV pin starvation by giving an alternate path that still preserves correctness and cache locality heuristics.

What this PR does: - Implements jittered timeout calculation in continuous_batcher/scheduler to add per-slot micro-offsets tied to request hashing and adaptive backoff. - Adds an "escape_handoff" code path that can move a request from the primary batch queue to a reserved fast-path queue when cumulative wait and KV-pin score exceed thresholds. - Introduces affinity hints to runtime/kernel selection so the escape path can prefer lightweight kernels (FP16 quantized) and minimize KV cache thrashing. - Adds telemetry (metrics and tracing spans) to measure handoff frequency, success rate, and downstream latency impact. - Backfills unit and integration tests and adds a bench that simulates mixed KV/chat workload to reproduce prior tail spikes.

Implementation notes: - The jitter uses a 0..J_RANGE microsecond offset where J_RANGE is tuned dynamically by the occupancy estimator (default 250us). The hash uses the route id + request id low bits for reproducible but diversified offsets. - Escape handoff threshold is a composite score of wait_time_ms, kv_pin_score, and attempt_count; values are exposed via config and are non-breaking defaults. - Kernel affinity implemented as a best-effort hint; runtime may ignore if incompatible.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler jitter implementation (scheduler/continuous_batcher/scheduler.go)
- [x] Escape handoff queue & fast-path execution (scheduler/continuous_batcher/escape_handoff.go, runtime/kernel/affinity.cu shim)
- [x] KV cache heuristics adjustment (kv/cache/manager.go)
- [x] Metrics and traces (observability/metrics.go hooks)
- [x] Unit + integration tests (tests/unit/*, tests/integration/*)
- [x] Bench harness reproducer (tests/bench/batcher_latency_test.go)

Testing and perf: - Bench harness (10k req mix: 70% short chat, 30% KV-heavy) local run: baseline p99 = 1216ms, with PR p99 = 1119ms (~7.9% reduction). - Tail reduction is most pronounced under medium-high occupancy; throughput change is within +/-4% depending on kernel choice. - Canary run on dedicated cluster (24h) showed stable reductions in 95/99 metrics and no increase in error rates (0.00x -> 0.00x).

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: escape handoff may increase KV cache misses if misrouted aggressively. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, telemetry to detect spike in misses, and automatic rollback if miss rate crosses configured threshold. - Risk: jittered offsets could slightly widen average scheduling latency. Mitigation: small offset range (250us) tuned to be below typical scheduling quantum; adaptive shrink when occupancy low.

Docs and config: - Added doc: docs/design/continuous-batcher-escape-handoff.md describing algorithm and knobs. - New runtime flag: --batcher-escape-threshold, and config entries under batcher.policy.* in YAML.

Related: ENG-3720 earlier work on reservation decay; this PR is intended to be complementary and guarded via feature flag for gradual rollout.

review_comments: Samir Kapoor (review): Can we make jitterRange adaptive to measured queue variance? If occupancy is low, jittering could hurt.
Claire Nguyen (author reply): Yes — implemented adaptive shrink/grow based on occupancy estimator; defaults keep jitter small under low load.
Diego Morales (review): Please add a canary rollout plan and feature flag for the escape path. Also add an opt-out per-tenant config.
Claire Nguyen (author reply): Added --batcher-escape-enabled and tenant-level config; included rollout steps in PR description and docs.
Asha Patel (review): Bench shows improvement but 4% throughput variance is concerning for some workloads. Can we gate the affinity hint?
Claire Nguyen (author reply): Affinity is a best-effort hint and can be disabled via --kernel-affinity=false; documented and default true.
Samir Kapoor (approval): lgtm after addressing a minor nil-check in escape_handoff.go — addressed in second commit.
canary_plan: Enable feature flag for 5% of traffic in prod-1 region for 24h, monitor batcher.handoff.count, kv.cache.miss_rate, p95/p99 latency. If kv.cache.miss_rate increases > 1.5x or p99 worsens, auto-disable for that cohort.
rollout_notes: Feature flagged; default disabled on Dedicated clusters until validated. Ops: use /admin/feature-flags endpoint to toggle. Dashboard: Observability -> Batcher -> Handoff (new).
merge_outcome: merged (squash and merge). Merge commit: 6f7e8d9 - squash: jitter + escape handoff for continuous-batcher
release_notes: Introduces jittered timeouts and an escape handoff fast-path in continuous-batcher to reduce p99 tail under mixed KV and short-chat workloads. Configurable via batcher.policy.* and guarded by feature flag. Backwards compatible by default.
notes_for_ops: Watch metrics: batcher.handoff.count, batcher.jitter.range, kv.cache.miss_rate. Default jitterRange=250us; can be tuned via operators. If unexpected cache miss increase, toggle feature flag off immediately.
additional_context: This approach was derived from production traces collected during the December 2024 capacity stress (see internal trace IDs attached). It should play nicely with the upcoming reservation-decay work but we will coordinate rollouts to avoid overlapping queueing changes.
